title: Capacity: full, half full, empty
examples: Teacher, how do I know if it is half full?
Can we use water to show what empty means?
If I pour from this cup to that cup, what happens?

explain.say: Watch me pour the water from this big jug. Now it is full.
Now I pour some out. See? It is not full, but it is not empty either. It is half full.
If I pour all the water out, there is nothing left inside. We say the jug is empty.
Now let us compare two cups. Which cup do you think can hold more water?

faq.q: What does it mean if something is empty?
faq.a: It means there is no water or sand inside it at all. You can see nothing inside the container.
asks: Is empty the same as nothing?
What is the opposite of full?

faq.q: How can I show something is half full?
faq.a: You can fill it up until it reaches the middle line. This shows it has the same amount in and out.
asks: What is half of a cup?
Can you show me half full?

faq.q: When we pour, what are we doing?
faq.a: Pouring means carefully moving liquid from one container to another. We watch where it goes.
asks: What is the action of pouring?

faq.q: How do I know which container holds more?
faq.a: You can pour water from both containers into a big tub. The one that fills the tub more holds more.

faq.q: Is it always easier to see if something is full?
faq.a: Yes, it is easiest to see when it is completely full. You can see the water right up to the top.
asks: Is full the easiest to check?
Can you tell if it is full?

facts: Full means the container has the maximum amount inside.
Empty means the container has zero amount inside.
Half full means the container has an equal amount in and out.
We use pouring to move liquid from one place to another.

quiz.say: If a bottle is completely full, can you pour any more water into it?
quiz.why: When it is full, there is no space left for more water to go.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might think it can hold just a tiny bit more.
wrong.1: This is tempting because it is vague, but 'full' means no more space.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might think water can always fit.

quiz.say: If you pour water from a small cup into a large jug until the jug is full, what is the small cup now?
quiz.why: Because you poured all the water out, the small cup is now empty.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might think you only poured half the water.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might think the water stayed in the cup.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it uses confusing words for the amount left.

quiz.say: Which container holds the most water, a small bowl or a large bucket?
quiz.why: The bucket is bigger, so it has more space inside to hold water.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it suggests the water changes the container's capacity.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it is easier to lift and move.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might think size does not matter.
